messages:
alex: quick brain-dump — before I draft the RFC, want to sync on whether we build a token/prefix coalescer layer (merge concurrent identical fetches) or iterate on lease-splitting for fairness. listing pros/cons to avoid rework.

maria: tl;dr: coalescer = fewer backend hits for hot prefixes but extra queue/joins. lease-split = better tenant isolation but can make many small leases and thrash eviction.

kevin: agree. add failure modes: coalescer can cause head-of-line blocking, harder attribution of costs, and GC complexity for join handles. but it can cut backend QPS a lot for identical reads.

jen: SRE note: if we coalesce we must preserve tracing/attribution. we need a coalesce_id in spans and a way to bill/journal cost per-originator. without that, telemetry/billing/forensics broken :grimacing:

maria: proto idea:
```
coalescer.join(prefix, req_meta):
  if inflight[prefix]:
    attach req to future
  else:
    start backend fetch, publish result to waiters
  on cancel: remove waiter
```
backpressure + per-tenant opt-out required.

kevin: correctness worry: read-after-write ordering. if a write happens while a long-running backend fetch is inflight, joiners might see stale data. contract options:
- make coalescer read-only and skip for read-after-write-sensitive flows
- add sequence checks so joiners can opt to wait for a later write

alex: proposal: coalescer only for pure reads (prefix fetches flagged no-write-intent). any request with write hint bypasses it. keeps semantics simple and safe.

jen: operational fallback: coalescer amplifies tails — if the primary fetch is slow we can fast-fail joiners after X ms to serve stale local read or try an alternative replica. need thresholds and alerts.

maria: eviction interaction: coalesced responses may re-pop an entry right after eviction, causing a small re-pop storm. that's acceptable if we surface metrics `repop_from_coalesce` so SRE can watch.

kevin: interface boundary suggestion: runtime exposes fetch contracts: `fetch_strict(prefix, caller_meta)` and `fetch_stale_ok(prefix, caller_meta)`. coalescer sits above and chooses which to call based on request flags.

alex: testing plan:
- unit: join/cancel logic, race us with evict
- integration: canary in staging, opt-in flag per-tenant
- load: synthetic hotkey to measure QPS savings vs eviction churn

jen: add alertable metrics: p50/p95/p99 for coalesce join latency, percent of joiners that fast-failed, and billing attribution gaps. set p99 threshold + auto-disable if regression.

maria: perf target: coalescer overhead <~2ms p50. start opt-in, flip on for low-risk customers first.

kevin: rollout plan: prototype (2w) limited to identical headers+prefix, evaluate. if wins, RFC for wider semantics.

alex: OK. I'll draft RFC with semantics, API sketch, metrics, rollback. action items: @maria prototype, @kevin tests & perf harness, @jen SRE metrics + alerts. I'll add a short-lived canary and a kill-switch.

prefetch-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/kv-coalescer-proto -> staging 2026-03-22T02:30:00Z

jen: noted. will watch canary dashboard and set an emergency pager rule for p99 tail increase.

maria: one more thought: tenant opt-out should be a soft header so proxies can set it for enterprise customers concerned about strict quota semantics.

kevin: also document that coalescer does not change eviction invariants; it's purely a request-side optimization. any re-pop is treated like normal writes for eviction accounting.

alex: sounds good. RFC draft by EOD Monday. thanks all :thumbsup:
